circāmoerĭum , ii, n. circa-moerus, for murus; cf. pomerium,
I.the space about a wall, on both sides of a wall: pomerium, verbi vim solam intuentes, postmoerium interpretantur esse; “est autem magis circamoerium,” Liv. 1, 44, 4 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
